title: Work IQ: long-running tasks for A2A and MCP agents
summary: The roadmap facts, billing model and documented control paths and commands are supported. Minor improvements should explain automatic service-principal provisioning, complete the group-policy creation guidance and add table coverage for the checklist's service-selection and alert controls.

claims.where: front matter: licensing.notes; Cost and licensing

claims.where: front matter: licensing.model; licensing.notes; Cost and licensing

claims.quote: You pay for use of the Work IQ API through a consumption-based model that uses Copilot Credits.

claims.claim: Microsoft 365 Copilot licensed users incur usage-based billing for custom and third-party agents using Work IQ.
claims.quote: For Microsoft 365 Copilot licensed users, Work IQ is available in all Microsoft 365 Copilot experiences and agents. It is subject to usage-based billing for custom and third-party agents.

claims.claim: Users without a Microsoft 365 Copilot licence are billed for Work IQ based on usage.
claims.quote: Users without a Microsoft 365 Copilot license are billed based on usage.

claims.where: controls[1].note; Cost and licensing; Governance controls
claims.claim: Spending policies set access and spending limits but do not reserve or allocate credits.
claims.quote: Spending policies control access and spending limits; they don't reserve or allocate credits for a workload, user, or group.

claims.where: controls[1].governs; Cost and licensing; Governance guidance: Before rollout
claims.claim: Work IQ API can be included in or excluded from a spending policy.
claims.quote: Include Cowork and exclude Work IQ API from a policy when its users shouldn't consume credits through Work IQ API.

claims.claim: Excluding Work IQ API from one policy does not exclude it from other applicable policies.
claims.quote: Review all applicable policies, including the default policy. Excluding a service from one policy doesn't exclude it from other policies.

claims.claim: The monitoring guide says a running task in a group policy can complete without interruption after exceeding the user's per-user limit.
claims.quote: Users in a group spending policy that exceed their per-user spending limit: If a running task exceeds the per-user limit, it can complete without interruption.

claims.claim: The monitoring guide says this excess usage does not count toward the policy limit.
claims.quote: The excess usage doesn't count toward the policy limit, isn't billed (at Microsoft's sole discretion), and doesn't appear as consumed credits in the Cost Management dashboards

claims.where: controls[1].ui; Governance controls table; Governance guidance: Before rollout
claims.claim: Create a spending policy under Microsoft 365 admin center > Copilot > Cost Management > Configuration > + Add spending policy.
claims.quote: In the Microsoft 365 admin center, go to Copilot > Cost Management. ... Select the Configuration tab and then select + Add spending policy.

claims.claim: POST https://graph.microsoft.com/beta/copilot/costManagement/spendingPolicies creates a spending policy.
claims.quote: For a group-scoped policy, follow the safe-create sequence: create the policy disabled, link its audience with Add assigned group, and let the service enable it once its requirements are satisfied.
claims.fix: Extend the note to explain that the printed create call alone does not attach a group: create disabled, then use the reference page's Add assigned group operation. If supplying nonempty assignedGroups during creation instead, also request CopilotCostManagement-Assignment.ReadWrite.All.

claims.claim: Creating a spending policy without an initial audience uses delegated CopilotCostManagement-Policy.ReadWrite.All.
claims.quote: Creating a policy without an initial audience (`assignedGroups` omitted or empty) requires only `CopilotCostManagement-Policy.ReadWrite.All`.

claims.claim: The spending-policy create API also requires Billing Administrator or Global Administrator.
claims.quote: At runtime, creating a policy also requires the Billing Administrator or Global Administrator directory role.

claims.claim: The create body requires a concrete @odata.type, displayName, periodLimit, perUserLimit and serviceSettings.
claims.quote: In the request body, supply a JSON representation of a spendingPolicy object with a concrete `@odata.type`. Required properties are `displayName`, `periodLimit`, `perUserLimit`, and `serviceSettings`.

claims.claim: The Graph create operation creates the policy disabled.
claims.quote: A new policy is created `disabled`.

claims.claim: The service-usage API requires exactly one completed UTC day per request.

claims.claim: The service-usage API is general service reporting, not a long-running-task-specific report.
claims.quote: Get a list of costManagementServiceUsageRecord objects that report each governed service's share of the tenant's consumption of Copilot Credits for one completed UTC day.

claims.claim: Spending policies support policy and per-user limits.

claims.claim: Learn does not confirm spending-policy evaluation specifically when a long-running task resumes.
claims.quote: Searched: Work IQ A2A task delegated token lifetime resume policy spending policy audit events administrator cancel other users tasks. Opened spending-policy management, consumption monitoring and A2A overview; no task-resume evaluation rules.

claims.claim: The cited Cost Management Graph APIs are beta, subject to change and unsupported in production applications.
claims.quote: APIs under the `/beta` version are subject to change. Use of these APIs in production applications is not supported.

claims.claim: Service-principal creation provisions Work IQ generally rather than switching on only long-running tasks.
claims.quote: This section creates the Work IQ service principal in your organization, which provisions the Work IQ resource so your applications can request tokens for it.

claims.claim: Microsoft has not confirmed that the documented MCP policy also governs A2A or this long-running-task feature.
claims.quote: Searched: Work IQ MCP tenant policy settings API Graph PowerShell Allowed Disallowed; "Work IQ" "A2A" "enable" "tasks" policy default. Opened MCP policy governance and A2A overview; policy applicability is documented for MCP tool requests, not A2A tasks.

claims.where: Governance guidance: At rollout; Governance controls table
claims.claim: The checklist's Auto-apply new services and email-alert controls lack explicit table coverage.
claims.quote: Checklist: "Turn off Auto-apply new services" and "Set per-user and policy limits and alert recipients". The spending-policy row describes limits and service selection, but not automatic service inclusion or alerts.
claims.fix: Add explicit coverage for automatic inclusion of new services and spending-threshold email alerts, either as rows or by expanding the spending-policy row. Use the existing spending-policy management source and its Select agents and services and Set limits and alerts sections.
